meta.purpose: Show a CEO where AI can move their pipeline, where process has to come first, what the gaps cost in their own numbers, and what to build first.
meta.promise: See where your pipeline is leaking value, where AI can help, and what to build first.
meta.pov: AI fails in commercial work when it is done fast, without governance, on work that doesn't matter. Process comes first.
meta.honestLabel: Your view of the work you know.
meta.disclaimer: An indicative self-assessment of your view of the work you know. Not a benchmark or an audit. Every figure is your own estimate, multiplied out; we add no industry averages.

workstreams.name: Origination and site

moves.processMove: Agree one site screening checklist and one go/no-go template for new sites, and use them on every site reviewed this month.
moves.aiMove: Point AI at your screening checklist so it pre-fills each site summary from your own data. Keep the go/no-go decision human.
moves.scaleMove: Measure hours per site screened before and after, then extend the AI step to early feasibility.

workstreams.name: Development: consent and grid
workstreams.help: Planning and consent, grid applications and offers, surveys

moves.processMove: Set up one tracker for every consent and grid milestone across the pipeline, with an owner and a next date for each.
moves.aiMove: Use AI to draft consent and grid status updates from your tracker, and to compare each new grid offer with the last one.
moves.scaleMove: Measure days from milestone to status update, then extend the AI step to the next consent or grid workstream.

moves.aiMove: Use AI to draft bid sections only from your approved answer set, with a named reviewer and a source check on every claim.
moves.scaleMove: Measure time to first draft and review findings, then carry the approved answer set into the next round.

questions.use: Scored privately into need, maybe or want (see urgency). Never shown to the user as a label or judgement. Drives which CTA is primary and is stored as ar_urgency.

notSure.label: Not sure
notSure.hint: Not sure? Choose it. It doesn't count against you.

scoring.gridIndex: Per workstream: processIndex = round((P - 1) / 3 * 100) and aiIndex = round((A - 1) / 3 * 100), so levels 1 to 4 give 0, 33, 67, 100. Not sure (0) gives null.
scoring.processMaturityIndex: round(mean of answered processIndex). Null if no workstream answered.
scoring.aiUseIndex: round(mean of answered aiIndex). Null if none answered.
scoring.ladderIndex: M1: 1 to 4 gives 0, 33, 67, 100; Not sure null. Reported, not used in readiness.
scoring.likert: Item score: positive = answer - 1; reverse = 7 - answer (0 to 6). Not sure excluded. Score = round(sum / (6 * answered) * 100).

foundations.facetRule: Facet score needs both items answered, else null.
foundations.balance: 3 positive and 3 reverse, one of each per facet: all-agree, all-disagree and all-neutral each score 50.

grow.balance: 2 positive and 2 reverse: all-agree, all-disagree and all-neutral each score 50.

bands.name: Untapped
bands.line: Growth from AI is not on the table yet. That is a sensible order: fix the workstreams that leak value first, then come back to this.

bands.name: Within reach
bands.line: Some of the ingredients to grow differently are in place. What is missing is one named offer or scope step, and a small test with a real buyer.

bands.name: Ready to test
bands.line: You have the appetite and the raw material to grow differently. The next step is one offer or scope step, one buyer, one test, with the rules in place first.

grow.nullLine: You chose Not sure on most of these, so we can't size this yet. A good question for your leadership team: what could AI let us offer, or take on, that we can't today?

readiness.label: AI readiness
readiness.formula: round(weighted mean of available components: processMaturityIndex x 0.4, foundations x 0.4, aiUseIndex x 0.2). Weights re-normalised over the components that are not null. Null if all are null.
readiness.display: Shown as a number with its zone label (Needs work, Getting there, Strong). Never a nickname.

scoring.weakness: Per workstream: weakness = 100 - (0.6 x processIndex + 0.4 x aiIndex), with a null index counted as 50. Process carries more weight because process comes first.
scoring.priority: priority = importance[goal] (1 to 3, from workstreams[].importance) x weakness.
scoring.biggestGap: Null when every workstream is Not sure on both process and AI (nothing known). Otherwise highest priority. Ties: higher importance, then lower processIndex (null counts as 50), then workstream order. If the top two priorities are equal after rounding, set jointWith to the second and say 'joint biggest gaps' on screen.
scoring.statusOrder: First matching rule wins, in the order listed.
scoring.fixProcessFirst: List of workstreams with P 1 or 2, whatever the AI answer, ordered by priority.
scoring.quickWins: List of workstreams with P 3 or 4 and A 1 or 2 (or Not sure), ordered by priority.

visibilityNote.when: 3 or more included workstreams have P = 0
visibilityNote.line: You chose Not sure on several workstreams. For a leader, that is a finding: ask each workstream lead how the work is done today and where AI is used.

value.principle: Every figure is the user's own estimate multiplied out. No benchmarks, no industry averages. Ranges, not points, with a midpoint.
value.midpoint: Band midpoint = (low + high) / 2; open-ended band uses its low value and the figure shows as 'at least'. A product uses the product of midpoints, the product of lows and the product of highs.
value.time: hours = K1 x K2 x 46 (K1 exact replaces the band with [n, n]); fte = hours / 1725.
value.slips: weeks = K3 x K4 (K3 None gives 0; K4 skipped).
value.optimise: Optimise pot = weeks / 4.33 x slipMonth. Plus, only if the user adds a people cost on the result page: hours / 1725 x cost per full-time person per year. Shown as 'about {mid} a year ({lo} to {hi})'.
value.grow: Grow pot = K6 x projectValue. Always labelled 'value at stake, not profit: you would not have won it all'.
value.severity: time = K2 severity; delay = mean(K3, K4) severity, 0 if K3 None; missed = K6 severity. Used for urgency only.

peopleCost.label: Add a people cost (optional): what one full-time person costs a year, salary plus overheads
peopleCost.use: Adds the time lost to the Optimise pot.

urgency.question: U1

levels.label: Maybe
levels.rule: No need option, and (nextquarter or notsure selected, or U1 unanswered, or the user's own cost answers are high: delay severity >= 0.4 or missed severity >= 0.5).

levels.label: Want
levels.rule: Only want options selected (strategic and/or nothing) and own cost answers are not high.

urgency.neverShow: Never show the level, its name or any wording that judges the user's urgency. The only visible effects are which CTA is primary and, for need, an echo of the user's own words.
urgency.echoTemplate: You told us that if nothing changes in the next 30 days, {echoList}.

develop.line: Approved, dated, owned evidence for consent and grid, with source links, feeding every application and submission.
develop.status: Set up with you on your own documents during a sprint.

win.line: A requirement and compliance matrix from the round rules, drafts cited to approved evidence, completeness and consistency checks, and human sign-off at every gate.

rule: 1. If Foundations data governance facet < 40 OR leadership and accountability facet < 40: 'governance' first, then the module for the biggest gap workstream as 'then'.
2. Else, sector ipp: the module for the biggest gap workstream (find, develop, win, buy, close).
3. Else, other sectors: 'win' if the biggest gap is win (bids apply to every sector); otherwise 'map' naming the workstream.
4. No biggest gap (all workstreams Not sure on process and AI): 'map'.

sprint.showWhen: sector = ipp AND the build-first module (or its 'then') is buy or close
sprint.h3: How it would start: a First Close Sprint
sprint.line: A First Close Sprint sets up the Close Desk on one of your live procurements, inside your own Microsoft 365, in 3 weeks: map, build, run, hand over. AI reads and checks. Your people decide.
sprint.price: Fixed price from GBP 14,000, excluding VAT.
sprint.priceRule: Only when SHOW_PRICE is true. Never show founding prices or refund terms.

rule: 30 days: biggest gap workstream. Status fixprocess or aiahead: its processMove. quickwin: its aiMove. scale: its scaleMove. unknown: moves.ask.

60 days: the lowest Foundations facet below 70: its facet move. If every facet is 70 or more (or null), the top quick win other than the 30-day workstream: its aiMove. Else the next fix-process-first workstream: its processMove. Else the next-ranked workstream: its scaleMove.
90 days: the goal move. If readiness is 70 or more and Grow band is ready or within: the grow move instead.

facet.leadership: Write down the one or two results AI must improve this year, who owns each, and which decisions AI may inform but never make, such as a bid price or an investment decision.

goal.pace: Measure the hours one pipeline stage takes today against day 1, and use that number to decide where the next change goes.
goal.round: Run the changed workflow on one section of the next submission as a practice, and fix what the review finds before the window opens.
goal.close: Map the path from today to financial close on your lead project, mark where work waits and for whom, and point the next change at the longest wait.
goal.scope: Write one page on the scope or market you want to add: which workstreams it stretches, and which change in this plan makes it possible with the team you have.

close.epc: Map the path from award to mobilisation on your next project, mark where work waits and for whom, and point the next change at the longest wait.
close.oem: Map the path from order to delivery on your next big order, mark where work waits and for whom, and point the next change at the longest wait.
close.services: Map the path from award to mobilisation on your next contract, mark where work waits and for whom, and point the next change at the longest wait.
close.other: Map the path from award to delivery on your next piece of work, mark where work waits and for whom, and point the next change at the longest wait.

moves.ask: Ask the lead of {wsName} two questions: how is this done today, and where is AI used? Then rate it again.
moves.grow: Pick one new offer or scope step from your Grow ideas and test it in one conversation with a real buyer, with the AI rules in place first.

who.direction: You sponsor it; name one owner in the team.
who.practice: You can start it this week; take the plan to your director by day 30.

governanceActions.rule: Report page 2: up to 3 actions, in this order, each only when its trigger is true.

items.when: FDG2 answered 5 to 7, or M2 is chat only
items.text: Move AI use off personal accounts onto an approved tool with company data protection, before the next submission.
Name an accountable owner for every AI-assisted document that leaves the business.
Publish a one-page 'what's allowed' guide: which tools, which information, who reviews.
Give your key documents one home and one owner each, starting with the workstream in your 30-day move.
Run one hands-on session on a real task with the people who do the work.
Agree in writing the one or two results AI must improve this year.
Where AI runs ahead of the process ({wsList}), agree the process and a named reviewer before using AI further.

governanceActions.fallback: If none trigger: 'Keep a quarterly review of AI use against your written results, owners and rules.'

leadTag.rule: Grow band ready, OR (Grow score 55 or more AND goal = scope). Private; HubSpot only.

goalContext.pace: Moving faster with the same team means the same few people carry more. The question is where their hours and weeks go now.
goalContext.round: The next round has a date that will not move. What matters is what is ready, checked and owned before the window opens.
goalContext.close: Financial close or a sale depends on procurement, contracts and lender or buyer questions landing on the same people at once.
goalContext.scope: More scope or a new market stretches the same team across new work, new rules and new partners.

round.epc: The next tender has a date that will not move. What matters is what is ready, checked and owned before it.
round.oem: The next supply contract has a date that will not move. What matters is what is ready, checked and owned before it.
round.services: The next contract has a date that will not move. What matters is what is ready, checked and owned before it.
round.other: The next bid has a date that will not move. What matters is what is ready, checked and owned before it.

close.epc: Getting won work to contract and mobilisation depends on supply chain, terms and handover landing on the same people at once.
close.oem: Delivering won orders on time depends on supply, production and terms landing on the same people at once.
close.services: Mobilising won contracts depends on terms, people and handover landing on the same people at once.
close.other: Getting won work into delivery depends on terms and handover landing on the same people at once.

report.leakH: What the gaps cost a year, in your own numbers
report.heatmapH: Your five workstreams: process and AI
report.heatmapCaption: Colour shows the level you chose: red Ad hoc or None, amber Some templates or Individuals, light teal Standard or Team, deep teal Measured or Integrated, grey Not sure.
report.ladderEcho: Across the business, you said: {ladderLabel}. Tools in use: {toolsList}.

find.pace: Every site screened by hand takes people away from the projects already moving.
find.round: Weak site data shows up later as weak bid evidence.
find.close: Site issues found late come back in due diligence.
find.scope: A bigger or new pipeline starts with screening more sites, faster, with the same people.

develop.pace: Consent and grid work is the long pole: when milestones are tracked by hand, dates slip without anyone deciding they should.
develop.round: Round eligibility rests on consent and grid evidence. If it is hard to find, the submission waits for it.
develop.close: Lenders test consent and grid status. Gaps found late move the close date.
develop.scope: Each new market or technology brings new consent and grid rules for the same team.

win.pace: Every bid rebuilt from scratch takes weeks the team could spend moving projects.
win.round: This is the work that wins or loses the round. Without one approved answer set, quality depends on who is free that week.
win.close: Commitments made to win the project become lender questions later.
win.scope: New offers and markets are won through bids. A standard bid process is what lets you go for more.

buy.pace: Comparing returns by hand is where procurement weeks disappear.
buy.round: Supply chain plans and local content commitments need procurement evidence ready before the window.
buy.close: EPC, module, turbine and BESS terms decide bankability. A late or inconsistent comparison moves financial close.
buy.scope: Building and owning means running more procurement yourselves, on the same team.

close.pace: Lender or buyer questions land on the same people who are moving the next projects.
close.round: Bankability evidence prepared once can support the round as well as the close.
close.close: This is the last step before money moves. Questions answered slowly or inconsistently move the date.
close.scope: Owning more projects means more closes, each with its own due diligence.
